indicators.note: almost means the phrase's synonym stops one letter short of its full length

parts.note: an account in the red has more taken out than is in it: overdrawn

explanation.surface: Someone stretching the truth while their bank balance is nearly negative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final N from OVERDRAWN. To overdraw a picture is to exaggerate it.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdraw is to depict something beyond its true proportions, an artist's word for overstating.

clue.text: Expression of content that's extremely satisfactory

parts.note: extremely is a synonym of very
satisfactory, as in 'all is well', means well

explanation.surface: A remark of contentment saying things are going excellently.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said to show agreement or satisfaction, a spoken sign of being pleased.

clue.text: Rearrangement, it's to do with paying

parts.note: re means concerning, to do with
settlement is the paying of a bill or debt

explanation.surface: A remark that some reorganisation is really about money.
explanation.definitionFit: Resettlement is moving people or things to new places, a kind of reorganisation.

parts.note: a row that is decaying would be putrid, and ... Row is a famous riding track in Hyde Park, London

explanation.surface: A line of houses falling into ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotten Row is a well-known bridleway in London's Hyde Park, which gives the question mark its point.
explanation.definitionFit: Something decaying is putrid or decomposing, the plain sense of the word.

clue.text: Interminably eerie means of river control

indicators.note: interminably here means without an end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: eerie means weird

explanation.surface: A spooky device for managing a river's flow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interminably' drops the last letter D of WEIRD.
explanation.definitionFit: A weir is a low dam built across a river to regulate its flow.

clue.text: Shouting for joy until jab injures

indicators.note: injures suggests damage, so the letters of the phrase are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: Someone cheering right up to the moment an injection hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injures' rearranges the eight letters of UNTIL JAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Being jubilant is being triumphantly happy, often loudly so.

explanation.surface: An instruction to skip meals in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast means rapidly as an adverb, and as a verb means abstaining from food.

clue.text: Principal supporter in a saloon perhaps

definitions.text: Principal supporter in a saloon perhaps

parts.words: Principal supporter in a saloon perhaps
parts.note: reads like the chief backer of a bar, but a car's head support is meant, principal suggesting head and supporter suggesting rest

explanation.surface: The chief patron of a bar or pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A saloon is a British name for a sedan car, not a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The cushion at the top of a car seat supports the occupant's head.

clue.text: Fit out, before time, the retinue

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: to fit out is to equip
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Instructions to kit out the entourage ahead of schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: An equipage is a carriage with its attendants, hence a train of followers.

explanation.surface: A woman glimpsed somewhere in view.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is a woman's name, and the iris is the coloured part of the eye used in seeing.

parts.note: ex means former, what once was
terminated means ended or finished

explanation.surface: Something reaching its end at the moment of its destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To exterminate is to wipe out completely, so the word means wiped out.

clue.text: Route from the heart of the country?

definitions.text: Route from the heart of the country?

parts.words: Route from the heart of the country?
parts.note: seems to mean a road from a rural interior, but an artery carries blood from the heart, so a main highway is meant

explanation.surface: A road leading out of the countryside's centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A main trunk road is named after the arteries that carry blood away from the heart.

explanation.surface: Something spoken firmly and with great belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conviction' means a guilty verdict, not strong belief: a judge pronounces punishment after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical string of words, and the punishment a judge pronounces after a guilty verdict.

explanation.surface: A woman who shows up ahead of someone named Beth.
explanation.walkthrough: Put this name before BETH and you get the full name Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, and the part of Elizabeth that precedes its last syllable.

indicators.note: during means within, so the letters lie inside the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: An actor being especially lively in the fourth act of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Being energetic is being lively and on the go.

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the letters are as heard rather than as written

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap; Lou is a short form of Louise

explanation.surface: A chilly woman named Louise was said to have dropped a suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue is a piece of evidence or suggestion pointing to a solution.

clue.text: It is just a stone's throw

definitions.text: It is just a stone's throw

parts.words: It is just a stone's throw
parts.note: sounds like a description of a short distance, but literally a device for hurling stones

explanation.surface: Somewhere very near at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A catapult is a forked stick with elastic for flinging small stones.

clue.text: Broke family getting in the way

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
kin means relatives, family

explanation.surface: Penniless relatives blocking the road.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is British slang for having no money.
explanation.definitionFit: Being broke means having no money, which is the slang sense.

parts.note: a match full of abuse suggests a quarrel, the familiar phrase for a shouting row being a match of that kind

explanation.surface: A sporting fixture marked by fierce abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: A slanging match is a British idiom for an exchange of insults.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurling abuse is what happens in this kind of row, so the word describes insulting talk.

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, so a gunner
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: A gunner entranced while doing his workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt means wholly absorbed or enthralled.

parts.note: seems to mean nimble movement in sport, but literally means treatment done on feet

explanation.surface: Skilful movement of the feet in dancing or boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: Care of the toenails and feet is a form of cosmetic treatment done on the feet.

indicators.note: ghastly suggests something horribly mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman described as an awful tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Teresa is a woman's name, so a lady.

explanation.surface: A young woman from a city Down Under.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of South Australia, and a girl's given name.

indicators.note: fanned means the letters are blown about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Fumes from a volcano that a man was blowing on.
explanation.walkthrough: Etna is a volcano in Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethane is a colourless hydrocarbon found in natural fuel deposits.

clue.text: One will put you in the picture

definitions.text: One will put you in the picture

parts.words: One will put you in the picture
parts.note: sounds like someone who informs you, but literally someone who takes your image

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps you informed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a camera records people in images, literally placing them in shots.

indicators.note: violently suggests the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A command to put in strenuous effort.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or artistic composition.

parts.note: E stands for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: A traveller from the East heads westward.
explanation.definitionFit: Anew means once more, afresh.

parts.note: taken as written
US is the abbreviation for under-secretary

explanation.surface: A heavy load placed on a junior minister.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a duty or responsibility, a load to carry.

clue.text: The French-American lady in Swiss city

parts.note: la is the French word for the
US means American
Anne is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A French-American woman living in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lausanne is a city on Lake Geneva in Switzerland.
